newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian gets five-year term for blasphemy.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian gets five-year term for blasphemy.

text.p: An Indonesian Moslem received a five-year prison sentence on Monday for blasphemy against Islam in a case that sparked a number of church burnings in eastern Java last month, a police spokesman said.
"He was sentenced to five years in jail in line with the prosecutor's demands," police Lieutenant Colonel Indra Agung told Reuters by telephone from the town of Situbondo.
Several thousand people had run amok following an earlier hearing last month in the trial of Mohammad Saleh.
At least five people were burned to death when the mob set fire to 25 Christian churches in the Situbondo area, about 160 km (100 miles) east of Indonesia's second city of Surabaya.
The Situbondo court house was damaged by the crowd, angered at the slow pace of the trial and rumours that Saleh had taken refuge in a church.
Blasphemy is a criminal offence in Indonesia.
Colonel Indra said security outside the Situbondo State Court during the one-hour hearing on Monday was tight and there was no trouble.
"We already prepared our security. It's all under control," he said.
Indra said police had asked Islamic groups to stay away from the court and had told Islamic schools to carry on as normal.
Police said early this month they had detained 54 people on suspicion of being involved in the Situbondo riot.
A number of churches in the Surabaya area were also attacked in June. Religious scholars have attributed the attacks to social and economic tensions in the area.
Moslems constitute the great majority of Indonesia's nearly 200 million people, but the government supports the separation of church and state and recognises the major religions.
